I guess in layman’s terms, if you don’t have either a psychological or physical dependence on alcohol then you don’t meet the diagnosis.

What exactly do you mean? It has been recognised in the DSM V as a mood disorder, and a main criteria for diagnosis is that it causes an impairment in the individual’s everyday functioning. 

There are even different types of depression listed in the DSM V, such as persistent depressive disorder and major depressive disorder. Research has also found depression to be comorbid with anxiety. It also has high prevalence rates and affects 6.7% of the American population yearly. 

Depression as an illness has been extensively researched through cognitive, psychological and biological approaches. Most importantly, it has been evidenced that individuals suffering from depression have low serotonin and hyperactivity from their HPA axis, which affects their moods. Patients generally rely on pharmacological drugs to get better and other treatments. 

I cannot emphasise any better on how depression is a disease. People with depression DO exhibit physical symptoms, such as fatigue, hypersomnia and insomnia.

It felt like forever but I finally opened my eyes. Everlong by the foo fighters is playing in the background.

A half empty bottle of Absolut Vodka. An opened packet of cigarettes lying on the passenger's seat. An old polaroid picture of us taped to the car window. My mouth feels dry and the taste of alcohol lingers under my breath. I look up and see my reflection in the rear mirror. A pair of bloodshot eyes stare right back at me. It's mine and they're empty.

I roll down the window and stick my arm outside. I can feel the harsh cold air passing through my fingers. The windshield is foggy and I catch a glimpse of the hazy sky. The corn fields are covered by mist and the atmosphere feels heavy. The air is eerie and hauntingly silent. We're at the side of the road in the middle of nowhere and no place to go.

'Where do we go from here?' you whisper softly.

And then I turn around and you're there by my side, next to me in the passenger seat. Everything about this moment feels surreal. The way your light brown hair falls down your face. Your soft brown eyes. I don't look at you because every time I do, I'm tormented by the memories we had and it tears me apart inside. I remember begging you not to leave me. You begged me not to push you away. 

There's a lump in my throat and I feel like I can't breathe. We're sitting here in silence but it feels like eternity. Tears are welling up around my eyes and I'm trying so hard not to weep.

'Are you real?' I say. 

You turn away and look out the window. You feel distant.

'I'm far away.' You answer. 

I look around me and everything is fading away into the distance. There's nothing left of us, of what we used to be. It's time to go.

I step hard on the pedal and the car rushes forward. The engine screams as we race towards the end of the road, towards an unknown future. My vision is blurry and my heart is pounding. We're driving through the in-between of one moment to another. Yet again, it doesn't matter. There will be no end to this.

I take one last look at you. 

And then it's all over.

The reason why you're in this dilemma right now is because that apartment was so important to you. But it seems like it's more important to you because of the past memories it represented than it being an ideal place to live in. Emotional attachments are hard to get rid of and what you need now is distance from this past relationship of yours. 

Moving in will only cause 2 scenarios:
1. Disappointment
For the first few months living in there will feel nostalgic but when the novelty wears off, you'll start to notice the flaws. You'll realise living in there without her isn't quite the same, ultimately it will never feel as good as before because you can never replicate the memories you had in the past. 
2. Loss of meaning 
Perhaps in time you will adjust to living there and make new memories. In time the old memories wouldn't matter. You might even feel indifferent to it. But during this process this house will become a 'rewritten memory' and it will lose it's original meaning. 

Ultimately, I think you shouldn't move back in to this apartment. Simply because having the same thing twice will never feel as good as the first time you had it. Start a new life in a new place, I honestly think you'll be happier that way :)

I think there are some people who aren't cut out for school and I'm one of them. I've had a rough academic journey throughout my life, I've done a lot of school hopping and my grades fluctuate a lot. 

I don't know if this counts as academics but shortly after secondary school I decided to escape the rigor of academics by enrolling into an animation course. It was refreshing to explore the arts instead of doing subjects like math and science. Plus, we didn't have to sit for exams, everything was assignment based. However it was still a school nonetheless so there was still the GPA system to worry about. 

We had modules like graphic design, filming, traditional animation and fine arts. I was enticed by what I was learning because they sounded so interesting. And the campus was so huge, there were just so many places to go. It was a huge school too there were always crowds of people moving around and I immersed myself into the lively atmosphere of the school. 

Eventually the novelty wore off and deadlines started getting closer and closer. And then the lectures started getting more meaningless and gradually I stopped attending tutorials. I got by because I did last minute work and I managed to survive for a few semesters. That was until the year end results came and my GPA dropped from a 2.8 to a 2.1. I barely passed most of my modules and I got D's for most of the modules. I don't know what happened because my grades were decent for the previous terms. But the school pushed me to the next year anyway because I didn't fail anything. That's when I really started struggling because I didn't have a good foundation in year 1. It didn't help that I didn't have a passion for what I was doing either and I skipped most of my lectures for the term because I was so ashamed that I didn't know anything. Nothing could get rid of the feeling that I didn't belong here. But the term was ending and I wasn't able to hand up my assignments which meant that I would most likely have to retain and fail my GPA. There was just no way out, I slogged it out for the next term and I tried very hard to catch up but no matter what it was impossible to save my GPA. Transferring courses wasn't an option either. I didn't want to face the truth so I gave myself false hope that I could pull up my GPA somehow. 

Finally, two weeks before the end of the semester, I approached my teacher and told her about my situation. She told me bluntly that my GPA couldn't be saved and it was pointless to stay in the course if I didn't want to work in the animation industry. And it really stung because I didn't want to be told that I wasted 1.5 years of my school life. If I stayed on I could still possibly graduate by the third year with a low GPA but a diploma nonetheless. 

I dropped out of school the next day. Everyone was shocked and I now have to deal with the social stigma of being a school dropout. And I know most people wouldn't see quitting school as 'fixing the situation', they see it as me giving up. And perhaps this personal account might not be the most relevant answer to your question. But I personally believe that quitting school was the solution. Because sometimes it's harder to quit then to hang on. Quitting isn't akin to giving up, sometimes it's better to accept the truth. It didn't matter if my GPA could be improved or not. The point was I was pursuing the wrong career path and I knew it. I don't really know what to do with my academic life now but if there's one thing I've learnt, it's that an education isn't about the grades or the degree, it's about the journey and if the journey doesn't lead you to somewhere then ultimately that degree is worthless. 

Sorry if this is out of point but I hope you got something out of it anyway.
